fieldMarks: Small, stout salamander about 9-10.7 cm long with white or light-grey crossbands across head, back and tail, hence 'banded salamander'.
Males are smaller with silvery-white bands that turn very white in the breeding season, and swollen cloacal glands; females are larger with silvery-grey bands.
behavior: Solitary and mostly nocturnal; lives under leaf litter or underground (to about 1 m) and may defend its burrow.

Breeds in late summer to fall (August-November), earlier in the north; females lay a single clutch of up to about 250 eggs in dry pond basins or depressions under cover and attend them until autumn rains flood the nest.
Larvae hatch in fall or as late as spring depending on flooding and metamorphose in spring or early summer; adults are inactive through most of winter.
habitat: Wooded habitats near swamps and vernal pools, including rocky bluffs, slopes and wooded sand dunes; more tolerant of dry conditions than most salamanders; adults entirely terrestrial.
range: NatureServe lists it across the eastern US from New Hampshire and Massachusetts west to Wisconsin, Missouri and Texas and south to Florida; it is not recorded for Canada in that source.
